title: F_3 HIP device kernel
description:
Implement the F_3 HIP device kernel for `permanent_bipedal3` on gfx1030, exposed via the FFI shim from T22.

## Background

The kernel is a HIP/ROCm implementation of the bipedal F_3 permanent for $n \le 63$ matrices (post 2026-05-15 user-approved CPU/GPU consistency narrowing — see Amendment 2026-05-15 (n-range) below), suitable for batch-permanent workloads where many independent matrices are computed in parallel on-device. The single-matrix Ryser walk is inherently sequential at the subset level; the GPU win comes from batching across matrices.

Block / grid sizing: one matrix per HIP block; threads within a block cooperate on fold_mul reduction. Bipedal `add`/`sub`/`mul` map directly to wavefront-wide `__ballot`/AND/XOR primitives.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `crates/gf2-kernels-hip/hip/permanent/permanent_bipedal3.hip` exists with the device kernel.
- [ ] [hard] On gfx1030, the kernel produces `permanent_bipedal3` values bit-identical to the CPU reference at the per-$n$ counts in Amendment 2026-05-15 (test-counts): $n=16$: 100 matrices, $n=24$: 100, $n=32$: 10, $n=40$: 1.
- [ ] [hard] Kernel signature accepts a batch of `M` matrices and outputs `M` permanents in a single launch.
- [ ] [hard] Tests gated `#[cfg(feature = \"hip\")]` and `#[ignore = \"external: gfx1030 device required\"]` (per CLAUDE.md test-tier conventions).
- [ ] [hard] `cargo build -p gf2-kernels-hip --release --features hip` succeeds.

## Amendment 2026-05-15 (test-counts) — user-approved per-n matrix counts

The original criterion 2 read: \"On gfx1030, the kernel produces `permanent_bipedal3` values bit-identical to the CPU reference on 100 random matrices for each $n \\in \\{16, 24, 32, 40\\}$.\" The kernel design (one matrix per HIP block with a sequential Gray walk in thread 0) makes the 100-matrices-per-$n$ contract infeasible at $n=32$ (~4G ops/matrix × 100 = ~6.5 hr) and $n=40$ (~1T ops/matrix × 100 = ~50 days).

**Replacement (user-approved via AskUserQuestion option A, 2026-05-15):** per-$n$ counts adjusted to:

| $n$ | matrices | rationale |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | 100 | ~6.5M ops × 100 = ~650M ops on gfx1030, ~seconds wallclock |
| 24 | 100 | ~16M ops × 100 = ~1.6B ops, ~minutes wallclock |
| 32 | 10  | ~4G ops × 10 = ~40G ops, ~tens of minutes |
| 40 | 1   | ~1T ops × 1 = ~1T ops, ~30 min on gfx1030 |

Bit-identity remains [hard]: every matrix that gets tested must produce CPU-identical output. Only the count contract is relaxed.

## Amendment 2026-05-15 (n-range) — user-approved CPU/GPU n ≤ 63 narrowing

The original Background section described the kernel as targeting `n ≤ 64` matrices, inherited from the CPU `permanent_bipedal3_singleword` contract. The 2026-05-14 reviewer flagged a u64 Gray-walk wraparound bug at n=64: with `upper = UINT64_MAX`, the loop `for (k = 1; k != upper; k++)` terminates *before* processing `k = UINT64_MAX`, silently dropping the all-elements subset for every 64×64 matrix.

**Replacement (user-approved via AskUserQuestion 2026-05-15, Option 1 \"Narrow both CPU and GPU to n ≤ 63\"):** the HIP kernel rejects `n > 63` at both the kernel body and the C host entry point. The CPU `permanent_bipedal3_singleword` / `permanent_bipedal3_singleword_simd` / `permanent_bipedal5_singleword` / `gray_code_iter` have been correspondingly narrowed to `n ≤ 63` for CPU/GPU consistency (committed in `afec59b9 refactor(jit:ae82bd73): narrow CPU bipedal3/5 to n ≤ 63`). The narrowing is wallclock-driven: 2^64 Gray steps takes ~600 years on either path, so the previous `n ≤ 64` contract was always implicitly bounded by feasibility.

The CPU multi-word path (`permanent_bipedal3_multiword`) is unchanged and now reachable at $n=64$ instead of $n=65$ via the dispatcher.
